newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Car imports into Saudi maintain downtrend.
newsitem.headline: Car imports into Saudi maintain downtrend.

text.p: Car imports into Saudi Arabia, the Gulf region's largest market, kept to their downtrend in 1996, falling by nearly two percent, a report by the Eastern Province Chamber of Commerce and Industry showed.

The report, quoted on Tuesday by the Arab News daily, said 115,000 cars were estimated to have been imported in 1996, down from 117,101 in 1995. This followed imports of 186,378 in 1994 and 254,152 in 1993.
Car imports into Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Arab states had soared with the return of consumer confidence just after the end of the Gulf War in 1991 which ended Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
But by 1993 imports started declining as lower oil prices until early 1996 put pressure on state spending, squeezed civil salaries and dragged down consumer confidence.
The Arab News said there were about 3.6 million cars on the road in the oil-producing kingdom last year.
